\section{Generated reference tables}\label{sec:gentables}
% ============================================================
%  Wrapper for the machine-generated reference tables.
%
%  Every \input below is produced by scripts/gen_report_tables.py
%  directly from the C++ source tree, so the tables track the code
%  rather than drift from it.  DO NOT edit the generated/*.tex files
%  by hand -- edit the source (or the generator) and re-run:
%
%      python scripts/gen_report_tables.py            # regenerate
%      python scripts/gen_report_tables.py --check    # CI drift guard
%                                                     # (NB: writes before
%                                                     #  it compares)
% ============================================================

The tables in this appendix are generated from the source tree by
\texttt{scripts/gen\_report\_tables.py}.  They are not maintained by hand: a
renamed flag, a new cycle-slip detector, or a changed state-key delimiter
appears here on the next run of the generator.  \emph{Known gap:} the
feature-flag table de-duplicates on the C\texttt{++} member name.  A
section master switch named \texttt{enable} in more than one config
sub-struct therefore appears once, and several \texttt{network.*} master
switches are absent.  The table is indicative.  The loaders
\texttt{GnssConfigLoad.cpp} and \texttt{GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp}
(\texttt{src/core/config/}) are authoritative, and the verdict on every key
the network loader reads (armed, recommended, kept off, unvalidated) is
recorded in \texttt{docs/CONFIG\_promotion\_ledger.json}.  The fragments
under \texttt{generated/} are git-ignored and rebuilt on demand
(\texttt{build.ps1 -Regen} / \texttt{build.sh -{}-regen}).
\texttt{gen\_report\_tables.py -{}-check} exits non-zero when a fragment
changed; it rewrites the fragments before comparing, so after a failed
check the regenerated tables are already in place.
